Amelia,

Thanks for sending — appreciated. Summary below, plus attached packet and a link to request read-only dashboard access. If you want, we can do a 20‑minute call to walk through live dashboards.

High-level answers (short):
- Uptime (availability): 99.95% standard for Hosted API (per your proposed tier). Computed as the percentage of successful 2xx responses from our inference frontends over a rolling 30‑day window, using 1‑minute buckets aggregated per-region and then weighted by request volume. Planned maintenance windows are announced and excluded per the agreement; emergency maintenance events are evaluated case-by-case for credits.
- Latency: We publish p50/p95/p99 token-emit latencies and request end‑to‑end latencies. Production SLA threshold is p95 < 350ms for small-text generation workloads (20–256 tokens). Latency SLOs are evaluated on a 30‑day rolling window; short-term incident detection uses 5‑minute sliding windows for alerting.
- Measurement & aggregation: Metrics are sampled at the request gateway (100% for metadata; payload sampling optional). Availability = (successful_requests / total_requests) per 1‑minute bucket. We then compute rolling percentages over 30 days. For latency histograms we use per-request latency and compute quantiles with HDR histograms; aggregation is across 1‑minute buckets, then computed over the 30‑day window.
- Sampling policy: By default we retain full request-level metadata (timestamps, status codes, model id, region) for 90 days at 1‑minute granularity. We retain 1‑minute aggregated counters for 13 months. Raw payloads are never stored beyond customer-configured retention.
- Alerting: Our ops playbook triggers an alert when a SLO breach condition is observed for N consecutive buckets (default N=3 for 1‑minute buckets), and we notify both Redwood Ops and the customer technical contacts via PagerDuty/email. We also support webhook hooks into customer incident systems and a curated SLA escalation path.
- Customer access: Nebula will receive read‑only Grafana dashboards (role-based invite), CSV export on request via secure S3 share, and an audit-grade timeseries export for the contracted retention window. Dashboards include raw 1‑minute series and pre-computed daily aggregates.
- Exceptions & temporary carve-outs: Short-term exceptions (e.g., scheduled maintenance beyond standard windows, short capacity constraints during migrations) can be requested via our Exception Request Form and require: dates, impact description, mitigation steps, and approver signatures. Exceptions are logged, and any SLA credits are handled per the contract. For exceptions >72 hours we require an operations mitigation plan and a canary rollout to minimize customer impact.

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Packet.pdf (contains sample Grafana screenshots, metric definitions, runbook excerpt)
Grafana dashboard invite: see attached invite file (Grafana_Dashboard_Invite.txt) — request the invite link and we'll provision read-only access.

Hi Amelia, Priya — looping in technical detail below.

1) Aggregation formula: our authoritative availability computation is a global ratio across the evaluation window. Concretely: for a given region and model set we compute total_success = sum_{t in 1m_buckets} successful_requests_t and total_requests = sum_{t in 1m_buckets} total_requests_t. Availability = total_success / total_requests over the 30‑day (720‑hour) rolling window. We provide both the bucketed per‑minute series and the global ratio so auditors can reproduce the calculation. We do not average per-minute percentages.

2) Raw timeseries export: available on request. For standard customers we can provision an S3 export of the requested 30-day window within 3 business days after authentication/approval. For regulated customers we offer expedited exports (24–48 hours) as part of an enterprise support addendum. Exports include timestamps, status code, model id, latency ms, request id (anonymized if requested), and region.

3) Retention options: default 13 months for 1‑minute aggregates; we offer a 24‑month option as an add-on for an additional fee (applies to aggregated series). Raw per-request metadata retention beyond 90 days requires a negotiated data residency/retention clause.

4) Exception form & credits: attached is a sample Exception Acknowledgement template we use internally. The SLA credit calculation is pro‑rata by the number of minutes below the SLO threshold across the evaluation window (example: a 2‑hour incident that reduces availability by 0.05% on a 30‑day window results in credit X equal to (baseline_rate - observed_rate) * monthly_fee * (minutes_affected / total_window_minutes); exact formula and minimum thresholds are in the contract Exhibit A). We'll send a redlined example for your procurement.

Operational notes: alerts trigger on N=3 consecutive 1‑minute failures by default; customers are notified on the first alert and given a status page update within 15 minutes. For planned maintenance we require a workback plan and at least 48 hours notice for exceptions to be excluded from SLO calculations.

Links & attachments: Exception_Acknowledgement_Template.pdf, SLO_Credit_Example.xlsx, runbook excerpt at https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSLORunbook
